newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE AND FEEDER CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE AND FEEDER CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO LOWER.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent lower, livestock analysts said.
Carryover selling was seen in live cattle following another sharp drop in boxed beef values Thursday and continued weakness in the fed cattle market, analysts said.
Boxed values fell $1.96 to $1.67 per cwt and fed cattle traded $2.00 lower for the week at $64.00.
Continued heavy deliveries against the August contract should also weigh on sentiment, they said.
Packers will likely lower bids to $63 for fed cattle to start next week, one analyst said.
Feeder cattle futures will likely follow the lead of live cattle, especially with another decline in the latest CME feeder cattle index.
However, calls for lower corn futures and the discount futures hold to the feeder cattle index may limit selling pressure, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.26 at $82.01 per cwt and August feeder cattle futures closed at 80.375 cents a lb on Thursday.
